items.title: The latest on FedRAMP 20x Phase 4
items.text:
This site is under development. :)

It shouldn't be public, but if you've stumbled across it, please stand by.

FedRAMP 20x entered Phase 4 on October 1, 2026. This phase is anticipated to last until March 31, 2027.

Phase 4 will be completed successfully when FedRAMP has performed at least 3 FedRAMP 20x Class D Pilot Certifications and finished the background research necessary to develop a new model for assessing physical datacenter and facility controls based on existing commercial certifications.

Monitoring Phase 4

FedRAMP will maintain this web page during Phase 4 as the primary source of truth for all Phase 4 activities. It will always show the latest dates and information. You may see dates or information in RFCs, Community Updates, Blog Posts, or other sources that have been overcome by events, but the dates on this page should always reflect FedRAMP's current goals.

items.title: The 20x Class D Cloud-Hosted Pilot
items.text:
This pilot will test the expansion of FedRAMP 20x requirements for cloud-hosted services to FedRAMP's highest current level of assurance - Class D (High). The goal of this pilot is to complete at least 3 FedRAMP 20x Class D Certifications against the pilot requirements.

The specific rules will be posted here after they are finalized.

items.title: Eligibility
items.text:
This will be open only to cloud service offerings that have applied for a CR26-compliant FedRAMP 20x Class C Certification prior to December 1, 2026.

Pilot participants who apply prior to December 1, 2026 will be disqualified from the pilot if they fail to receive a positive determination before February 1, 2027, due to gaps in their application package.

items.title: 20x Class D Pilot Rules
items.text:
20x Class D requirements are currently open for public comment!

RFC-0036 FedRAMP 20x Class D Cloud-Hosted Pilot Requirements contains the proposed requirements for the 20x Class D pilot. These requirements will change after public comment, but the RFC shows the anticipated scale and scope of increased assurance expectations for 20x Class D.

items.title: Self-Hosted Industry Engagement
items.text:
To enable maximum speed and widest adoption, FedRAMP 20x Phase 1-3 focused exclusively on developing an updated path for cloud services that were hosted on infrastructure or platforms that were already FedRAMP Rev5 Certified. This provided a path for the majority of cloud services, but de-prioritized a path for the rare services that operate their own physical infrastructure.

FedRAMP plans to remedy this in the Consolidated Rules for 2027 by offering an expanded set of criteria for self-hosted or hybrid-hosted services to qualify for a FedRAMP 20x Certification of any Class. We understand that most companies who are responsible for their own infrastructure are already expected or required to meet stringent government regulations and commercial guidelines to operate datacenters safely. We anticipate leveraging those existing investments to the maximum extent possible.

There is now a single Industry Engagement track for Phase 4.

RFC-0033 Phase 4 Development Tracks for 20x Class D initially proposed 2 separate industry engagement tracks, one for cloud service providers and another for independent assessment services. We have reworked this into a single Industry Engagement track to ensure all activities align with the same schedule.

During Phase 4, FedRAMP will gather data and perspectives directly from current FedRAMP Certified cloud service providers with self-hosted or hybrid-hosted services and their independent assessment services. We will focus on industry standard certifications that are most widely used by these providers, and the deltas between those certifications and the requirements from existing FedRAMP Rev5. Our goal, where possible, will be to identify existing reusable certifications and classifications that can be included directly in a FedRAMP 20x Certification to address infrastructure-related controls.

FedRAMP will also publish at least 2 RFCs related to self-hosted and hybrid-hosted rules to ensure all stakeholders have the opportunity to participate.

items.title: Self-Hosted Industry Engagement Participation
items.text:
FedRAMP will engage with all stakeholders regarding self-hosted and hybrid-hosted requirements via the FedRAMP Request for Comment (RFC) process. The RFC processes ensures equal access and consideration for all stakeholders.

In addition, FedRAMP has offered the opportunity for direct engagement to a subset of key FedRAMP stakeholders as follows:

  • Cloud service providers with existing FedRAMP Certifications at Class C or Class D who have at least 15 agency uses on record by FedRAMP and appear to operate their own datacenter facilities based on the information readily available to FedRAMP. FedRAMP identified 12 qualifying cloud service providers and asked them if they would like to participate and 4 responded in the affirmative.

  • Independent assessment services that have assessed more than 20 total cloud service offerings. This is a change from RFC-0033 which proposed direct engagement only with independent assessment services of the qualifying cloud service providers. 8 independent assessment services will be asked to participate.
